questions.question: Which Grand Slam tournament was played between 17 to 30 January 2022?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Australian Open.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Australian Open** took place **at Melbourne Park, Australia** from **17 to 30 January 2022****.**
 
• It was the **110th edition **of the Australian Open and the first Grand Slam of the year.
 
• The **men’s singles** title was **won by Rafael Nadal,** who won his **21st major title** and **his second Australian Open**.
 
• The **women’s singles** title was won by **Ashleigh Barty**, who won **her first Australian Open title** and third major title.
 
• Barty was the first Australian to win the title since **Chris O’Neil won the title in 1978****.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__****Details of the other Grand Slam tournaments of 2022**

 
• 
 
**French Open**:

 
 
• The French Open was held at the **Stade Roland Garros in Paris, France, **from **22 May to 5 June 2022**.
 
• It was the **126th edition **of the French Open and the second Grand Slam event of 2022.
 
• The **men’s singles title** was won for the **14th time by Rafael Nadal**, who won his **22nd Grand Slam title****.**
 
• The **women’s singles title **was won by **Iga Świątek,** who won **her second French Open** and second grand slam title, having won her first at the 2020 French Open.
 
 
 
• 
 
**Wimbledon**:

 
 
• Wimbledon took place at the **All England Lawn Tennis and Croquet Club in Wimbledon, London, United Kingdom** from **27 June to 10 July 2022****.**
 
• It was the** 135th edition** of Wimbledon and the third Grand Slam tournament of the year.
 
• **Novak Djokovic **successfully defended his gentlemen’s singles title to claim his** 21st major title**, defeating Nick Kyrgios in the final.
 
• The l**adies’ singles title **was won by **Elena Rybakina**, who defeated Ons Jabeur in the final.
 
 
 
• 
 
**US Open**:

 
 
• The US Open took place at the **USTA Billie Jean King National Tennis Center in New York** City from **August 29 – September 11, 2022**.
 
• It was the **142nd edition **of tennis’ US Open and the fourth and final tennis major (Grand Slam event) of the year.
 
• **Carlos Alcaraz and Iga Świątek** won the **men’s and women’s singles titles**, respectively.
 
• **Carlos** became the** first male player from the 2000s** (born in 2003) and **Iga** became the** second female player from the 2000s** (born in 2001), to win the tournament’s singles titles.

questions.question: Why is PC Mahalanobis' name talked about in the context of Five-Year Plans?

options.text: He was the chairman of the Planning Commission.
He established the Institute of Economic Growth.
He conceptualised the framework for the Second Five-Year Plan.
He was the finance minister during the First Five-Year Plan period.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**He conceptualised the framework for the Second Five-Year Plan.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Prasanta Chandra Mahalanobis** was an **Indian statistician** who played a significant role in** formulating India's strategy for industrialization in the Second Five-Year Plan (1956–61).**
 
• The Plan, influenced by the Mahalanobis model, stressed the importance of **boosting the public sector's role **in the economy and targeted significant growth in sectors like **steel, electricity, and heavy machinery.**
 
• Although Mahalanobis was not the chairman of the Planning Commission nor the Finance Ministry during this time, his contributions were instrumental for the execution of the economic strategy during the Plan period.
 
• Therefore, his name is often mentioned alongside the development of these five-year plans in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** **Second Five year plan:**

 
• The Second Five-Year Plan, also known as the **Mahalanobis Plan**, was proposed by Indian statistician Prasanta Chandra Mahalanobis in 1955. It was in effect from **1956 to 1961.**
 
• This plan focused on the development of the** public sector** and aimed to create a socialistic pattern of society.
 
• This Plan set the precedence for a predominant role of the state which would determine the **direction of the economy.**
 
• A substantial part of the plan was focused on** increasing industrialization,** with a particular emphasis on the development of heavy industries such as **steel, heavy engineering, machine making, etc.**
 
• The Plan aimed at a** 25% increase** in the national income over a period of five years and a transformation in the pattern of industrial production.
 
• However, the Plan was only partially successful in achieving its objectives, and the target growth rate of **national income (5%) was not achieved. **Still, it set a clear path for future industrial policies in India.

questions.question: Which from the following is a phylum of animals found in fresh water ponds, lakes and swamps provides setae or parapodia for locomotion?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Annelida.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Annelida** is the phylum that includes **animals found in freshwater ponds, lakes, and swamps **that utilize setae or parapodia for locomotion.
 
• Examples of annelids include **earthworms, leeches, and marine worms.**
 
• This phylum includes around **22,000 species** of segmented worms.
 
• Annelids have bodies that are divided internally and externally into well-defined segments with** circular and longitudinal muscle fibres.**
 
• They exhibit a wide range of adaptations where they have evolved to be present in diverse habitats - **terrestrial, marine and freshwater **environments. Segmentation provides for such locomotory adaptability.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ctenophora:**

 
 
• Ctenophora, commonly known as **comb jellies,** represents a phylum of invertebrate animals that live in** marine environments.**
 
• They are characterized by their gelatinous bodies and the** 'combs,' or rows of cilia**, they utilize for movement.
 
• Contrary to some initial assumptions, they do not sting like jellyfish.
 
 
 
• **Porifera:**
 
 
• Porifera is the phylum that **includes sponges.** These are typically **marine animals,** though **some freshwater species** exist.
 
• They are known for their porous bodies and the fact that they are sessile, meaning **they attach themselves to the substrate and do not move around.**
 
• Sponges play a crucial role in marine ecosystems by** filtering water** and providing habitats for numerous small aquatic creatures.
 
 
 
• **Platyhelminthes:**
 
 
• The phylum Platyhelminthes includes **flatworms, such as tapeworms and flukes.**
 
• These animals are often** parasitic,** living at the expense of a host organism. They can be found in a variety of environments.
 
• Their bodies are dorsoventrally flattened, hence the name "flatworms," and they are bilaterally symmetrical

questions.question: Which autonomous body was operationalised under the Ministry of Surface Transport in 1995?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**National Highways Authority of India (NHAI).**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **National Highways Authority of India (NHAI)** is an autonomous body under the **Ministry of Road Transport and Highways**, Government of India.
 
• Operationalised **in 1995**, the NHAI is responsible for the management of a network of over 70,000 km of national highways in the country.
 
• It was given the mandate for the** development, maintenance, and management of National Highways, **which are the arterial roads of the country, designed for high-speed traffic.
 
• The NHAI is involved in the planning and implementation of various projects like the **National Highways Development Project (NHDP)**, which encompasses the **Golden Quadrilateral and the North-South and East-West Corridors.**
 
• It carries out highway projects through a model of **public private partnership (PPP) **in addition to receiving budgetary support from the central government.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Border Roads Organization (BRO):**

 
 
• The BRO is tasked with maintaining road networks in** India's border areas** and friendly neighbouring countries.
 
• It works under the **Ministry of Defence** and plays a crucial role in the **strategic and tactical movement of the armed forces.**
 
 
 
• **Centre for Railway Information System (CRIS):**
 
 
• CRIS is an autonomous organization under the** Ministry of Railways.**
 
• It develops and manages the critical Information Technology applications of the Indian Railways.
 
 
 
• **Inland Waterways Authority of India (IWAI):**
 
 
• IWAI is the statutory authority in charge of the** waterways in India** for the purpose of **shipping and navigation.**
 
• Its tasks include the development and regulation of inland waterways for shipping and navigation.
 
• It operates under the **Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways.**

questions.question: Micro credit or micro finance is a novel approach to bank with poor. In this approach bank credit is extended to the poor through _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**self-help groups.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Microfinance or microcredit** refers to the provision of **financial services, including loans, savings, insurance, and training **to people living in poverty.
 
• These services are typically targeted at underserved populations who do not have access to typical banking services. The approach is designed to support **entrepreneurship, empower poor individuals, and stimulate economic growth.**
 
• In this mode of operation, bank credit is extended to the poor through **Self Help Groups (SHGs)**, which are small voluntary associations of poor people created for the purpose of solving their common problems.
 
• SHGs usually consist of **10-20 individuals** from a homogeneous class who come together to pool their resources to cope with emergencies, provide **collateral-free loans** to members, and often serve as a conduit for formal banking services.
 
• This approach has proven successful in reaching large numbers of poor individuals, particularly women, and allowing them to partake in **income-generating activities.**

questions.question: Which state ranks first with a total length of 31.2 thousand km of rivers and canals, which is about 17% of the total length of rivers and canals in the country?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Uttar Pradesh.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Uttar Pradesh** ranks** first** in the country with a total length of** 31.2 thousand kilometers** of Rivers and Canals. This constitutes about **17%** of the total length of rivers and canals in India.
 
• The state is drained by two major rivers, the **Ganges and the Yamuna, **as well as a number of their significant tributaries such as the** Ghaghara, Gomti, Chambal, Betwa, and Ken.**
 
• Canals form an integral part of Uttar Pradesh's **irrigation system. **The Upper Ganges Canal, one of the oldest canals in India, and the Lower Ganges Canal are the lifeblood of swathes of agricultural land in the state.
 
• These rivers and canals play a critical role in supporting **agriculture**, which is the mainstay of the **state's economy, **providing necessary water for farming.
 
• The extensive network of rivers and canals also supports **fisheries and local commerce,** and holds cultural and religious significance, with towns like **Varanasi and Allahabad** being significant religious hubs due to their location on the banks of the** Ganga and Yamuna rivers **respectively.
 
• However, water management remains a significant challenge, with issues of drought in some areas and floods in others due to variable rainfall and limited storage capacity.

questions.question: Hindustan Copper Limited (HCL) was incorporated in the year _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1967.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Hindustan Copper Limited (HCL) **was incorporated on** November 9, 1967**.
 
• It is a **public sector** undertaking under the administrative control of the** Ministry of Mines,** Government of India.
 
• HCL is involved in **exploration, mining, beneficiation, smelting, refining and casting of refined copper metal.** It is India's only vertically integrated copper producer and is involved in a wide spectrum of activities in the metal sector.
 
• HCL's mines and plants are spread across four operating units, namely: **Khetri Copper Complex in Rajasthan, Indian Copper Complex in Jharkhand, Malanjkhand Copper Project in Madhya Pradesh, and Taloja Copper Project in Maharashtra.**
 
• It is also responsible for contributing to the supply of copper products, like copper cathodes, continuous cast copper rods, and other by products, such as **gold, silver, and sulphuric acid,** to the Indian market.
 
• In the recent years, HCL has been focusing on increasing its production capacity and upgrading its older mines and plants, demonstrating its commitment to the development of the nation's copper industry.
 
• As a leading copper manufacturer in the country, HCL plays a significant role in **India's metal industry, **influencing the country's industrial growth and contributing significantly to the nation's economy.

questions.question: Vajira Chitrasena of Sri Lanka was conferred the Padma Shri award 2020 for which of the following?

options.text: Enriching India-Sri Lanka ties through Indian classical dance
Enriching India- Sri Lanka ties through education
Enriching India- Sri Lanka ties through social work
Enriching India-Sri Lanka ties through Indian classical music

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Enriching India-Sri Lanka ties through Indian classical dance.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Vajira Chitrasena** is a renowned artist from **Sri Lanka.**
 
• She was awarded the **Padma Shri in 2020, **which is **India's fourth highest civilian honor.**
 
• Her key contribution was in the **field of dance.**
 
• Her work has played a significant **role in enriching the cultural environments of both India and Sri Lanka.**
 
• Through her **Indian classical dance**, she has strengthened ties between India and Sri Lanka.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Padma Shri award:**

 
 
• The Padma Shri award is one of the highest civilian honors in India, regarded as the **fourth highest**.
 
• It was instituted by the Government of India in **1954**.
 
• This award recognizes and appreciates distinguished contributions in various areas of activity such as **arts, education, industry, literature, science, acting, medicine, social service and public affairs**.
 
• The award holds a lower rank compared to **Bharat Ratna, Padma Vibhushan, and Padma Bhushan awards**.
 
• Every year, the awards are announced as part of the** Republic Day festivities in January, **and presented later by the **President of India**.
 
• Despite being primarily awarded to Indian citizens, the award can also be conferred upon **individuals of any nationality **who have contributed in a significant way to India or the broader Indian diaspora.

questions.question: Which pioneer scientist used radio waves to transmit signals over distances of several kilometres in the 1890s?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Guglielmo Marconi.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Guglielmo Marconi** was an** Italian inventor and electrical engineer.**
 
• He conducted pioneering work in **long-distance radio transmission.**
 
• Marconi developed a practical **radio wave-based wireless telegraph system** in the late** 19th century.**
 
• His system was able to transmit signals over distances of **several kilometers.**
 
• Marconi's contributions helped significantly expand the field of** telecommunications.**
 
• His work was recognized internationally when he was awarded the** Nobel Prize for Physics in 1909.​**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Michael Faraday:**

 
 
• Michael Faraday was a** British scientist **who contributed significantly to the field of** electromagnetism and electrochemistry.**
 
• He discovered **electromagnetic induction, diamagnetism, and the laws of electrolysis.**
 
• Although Faraday **discovered electromagnetic fields**, he did not work on radio wave transmission.
 
 
 
• **Paul Langevin:**
 
 
• Paul Langevin was a **French physicist.**
 
• He is known for his work in developing **Langevin dynamics and the Langevin equation.**
 
• He developed the use of **ultrasound** using piezoelectricity but wasn't involved in radio wave transmission.
 
 
 
• **Pierre Weiss:**
 
 
• Pierre Weiss was a **French physicist** known for his work in** magnetism.**
 
• He introduced the concept of magnetic domains, which helps explain the magnetic behavior in **ferromagnetic materials.**
 
• His main work was on magnetism, not on radio wave transmission.

questions.question: Which of the following states organises 'Lokrang', a five-day festival, beginning every year on 26 January?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Madhya Pradesh.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **'Lokrang'** is a prominent cultural festival held annually in **Madhya Pradesh.**
 
• The festival **begins** every year on **26th January.**
 
• This event has a **duration of five days.**
 
• 'Lokrang' showcases the rich traditional** folk dances and music** of the region.
 
• The festival exhibits a wide range of** cultural performances, including tribal dances, classical dances, dramas, and folk theaters.**
 
• It is an event that reflects the **vast cultural diversity of Madhya Pradesh** and offers an engaging cultural experience for visitors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__****Festivals of Other States:**

 
• **Arunachal Pradesh:**

 
 
• Arunachal Pradesh is known for its rich tribal culture with **26 major tribes** and numerous sub-tribes.
 
• The **Solung festival**, celebrated by the Adi tribe, is one of the most prominent in the state.
 
• The state is also known for traditional crafts like** weaving, wood carving, and pottery.**
 
 
 
• **Himachal Pradesh:**
 
 
• Himachal Pradesh hosts a variety of local festivals such as **Kullu Dussehra and Lavi Fair.**
 
• It's also renowned for its rich tradition in **folk dance and music**, such as the popular **Nati dance.**
 
• The **'Rampur Jatar' **is a well-known fair that displays traditional **folk art and craft.**
 
 
 
• **Uttar Pradesh:**
 
 
• Uttar Pradesh is known for its diverse culture and traditions.
 
• Festivals like** Diwali, Holi, and Eid **are celebrated with great fervour.
 
• **Kumbh Mela**, a large-scale Hindu pilgrim festival, is held in the city of Prayagraj (formerly Allahabad), attracting millions of devotees.
 
• Uttar Pradesh also has a rich tradition of classical **music and dance**, including **Kathak,** one of the eight classical dance forms of India.

questions.question: The art of decoration, called Pietra dura became popular during whose reign?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Shah Jahan.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pietra dura** is an intricate art form that involves **inlaying semi-precious stones into a stone base.**
 
• This form of decoration became highly popular during the reign of the** Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan.**
 
• Shah Jahan is famed for his patronage of arts and architecture, most notably, the **construction of the iconic Taj Mahal.**
 
• Pietra dura was **extensively used to embellish the Taj Mahal. **The floral patterns and detailed designs one can observe on the monument are excellent examples of this art form.
 
• The intricate work in Pietra dura reflects the high** level of craftsmanship** prevalent during Shah Jahan's period.
 
• Pietra dura continues to be appreciated today for its **aesthetic appeal and exquisite craftsmanship.****​**

**​** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Jahangir:**

 
 
• Jahangir was the fourth Mughal Emperor who ruled from** 1605 until his death in 1627.**
 
• He was known for his love of **art, culture, and architecture, **with a keen interest in natural history, which is reflected in many paintings from his era.
 
• Jahangir continued his father Akbar's traditions of encouraging art and learning but had a more refined taste, resulting in more detailed and nuanced artworks during his period.
 
 
 
• **Sher Shah Suri:**
 
 
• Sher Shah Suri was the** founder of the Suri Empire in India.**
 
• His reign from **1540 to 1545 **was marked by the implementation of several administrative reforms and the commissioning of significant infrastructural projects like** roads and inns.**
 
• Sher Shah's most famous architectural contribution is the **Old Fort (Purana Qila) in Delhi**, reflecting his commitment to civic utilities and effective administration.
 
 
 
• **Akbar:**
 
 
• Akbar was the third **Mughal Emperor**, ruling from **1556 to 1605.**
 
• Recognized as one of the greatest Mughal rulers, Akbar's reign was marked by advancements in **literature, art, and culture.**
 
• He commissioned prominent architectural projects, illustrating his dedication to art and culture. The city of **Fatehpur Sikri,** in particular, stands as a testament to Akbar's architectural prowess.
 
• Also, he introduced a unique **painting style known as the Akbari style**, intermingling Persian and Indian artistic traditions.

questions.question: The capital of Vajji Mahajanapada was __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vaishali.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Vajji **was an ancient Indian **Mahajanapada**, a federation of several republics, rather than a single kingdom.
 
• The federation of Vajji represents one of the world's earliest examples of a republic, dating back to the **6th century BCE.**
 
• **Vaishali**, also known as **Vesali or Vaiśālī **in ancient texts, was the capital of Vajji Mahajanapada.
 
• Located in **present-day Bihar,** Vaishali is of significant historical and archaeological importance.
 
• Vaishali is also revered in** Buddhism and Jainism** as it was a favourite place of Lord Buddha and the **birthplace of Lord Mahavir.**
 
• Today, Vaishali is known for its archaeological sites including **stupas, pillars, and ancient ruins** that reflect its rich past.

questions.question: In which year was the 1st winter edition of the Olympic Games organised?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1924.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **first Winter Olympic Games** were inaugurated in **1924.**
 
• The host city for these games was** Chamonix,** which is situated in **France.**
 
• These were the inaugural Winter Olympics in the history of modern Olympic Games.
 
• Originally, the event was called** "International Winter Sports Week" **and was considered a part of the 1924 Summer Olympics.
 
• However, they were** retroactively designated** as the **first Winter Olympics in 1926.**
 
• The 1924 Winter Olympic Games included sports like **speed skating, figure skating, hockey, curling, and various skiing events.**

questions.question:
Which of the following pair of compound - boiling point is correct?

I. Chloroform - 334K

II. Methane - 111K
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both I and II.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Chloroform **has a boiling point of **334K**. It is a **colourless, heavy, sweet-smelling, non-flammable liquid** that is used in a variety of industrial and laboratory applications.
 
• In the **human body,** it depresses the central nervous system and can cause effects ranging from **dizziness to unconsciousness. *Hence, match I is correct.***
 
• **Methane**, on the other hand, has a much lower boiling point of **111K**. Methane is a **colourless, odourless gas.**
 
• It's the main constituent of **natural gas**, which is used extensively in various industrial applications. It's also a significant greenhouse gas, with numerous environmental impacts. ***Hence, match II is also correct.***
 
• Boiling points are often used in chemistry as an indicator of the strength and types of forces among molecules in a substance. **Stronger intermolecular forces result in higher boiling points.**

questions.question: The Constitution (Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes) Order (Second Amendment) Bill, 2022 was passed by the Parliament. This is pertaining to the state of __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Uttar Pradesh.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The Constitution **(Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes) Order (Second Amendment) Bill, 2022 **was passed by the Indian Parliament.
 
• It is specifically related to the state of **Uttar Pradesh.**
 
• The bill modifies the Constitution **(Scheduled Castes) Order, 1950**, and the Constitution **(Scheduled Tribes) (Uttar Pradesh) Order, 1967**, both of which enumerate the communities recognized as Scheduled Castes (SCs) and Scheduled Tribes (STs).
 
• These changes pertain to the reclassification and inclusion of certain communities within the **SC and ST categories** in Uttar Pradesh.
 
• These amendments aim to provide relevant **benefits, reservations, and protections **under the Indian Constitution to the newly added communities.
 
• By acknowledging the **socio-economic challenges** faced by these communities, this bill seeks to uplift them through affirmative action.

__
 
• **Uppalapu Srinivas**, often referred to as **Mandolin Srinivas,** was a renowned **mandolin player** from India.
 
• He specialized in the field of **Carnatic classical music.**

• He was known for how he adapted the mandolin, a primarily western instrument, to the unique needs and nature of Carnatic music.
 
• Srinivas first picked up the mandolin at a young age and quickly gained** recognition as a child prodigy in music.**
 
• Over the course of his career, he won several awards for his contributions to music, including the** Padma Shri in 1998, **and left an indelible impact on Indian classical music.

questions.question: Which of the following committees recommended for the inclusion of fundamental duties in the Constitution of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Swaran Singh Committee.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Swaran Singh Committee** was established in **1976** under the leadership of Sardar Swaran Singh, an Indian Politician.
 
• The committee was specifically constituted to study and suggest changes to the Constitution in relation to the concept of** fundamental duties**. It was the Swaran Singh Committee that suggested adding** a new part outlining citizen duties.**
 
• As a result of this committee's recommendations, **the 42nd Amendment to the Constitution in 1976** included the new** Part IVA, **which specified the fundamental duties of Indian citizens. It comprises **Article 51A from (a) to (k).**
 
• The fundamental duties include tenets like respect for the **national flag, the constitution, and institutions, promoting brotherhood, protecting the environment, and upholding scientific temper among others.**
 
• The primary aim behind the inclusion of the Fundamental Duties by this committee was to create a** balance of rights and duties** in the constitution, obliging citizens to act responsibly and assist in maintaining the spirit of democracy in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sarkaria Commission:**

 
 
• The Sarkaria Commission was established in 1983 by the central government of India.
 
• The Commission was set up to examine the relationship and balance of power between state and central governments in the country and suggest changes within the framework of the Constitution.
 
• It made 247 recommendations to improve the efficiency, effectiveness, and balance between the various levels of government in India.
 
• The report of the Sarkaria Commission is the first and the most comprehensive attempt to review Centre-State relationship.
 
 
 
• **Rajamannar Committee:**
 
 
• The Rajamannar Committee was constituted by the government of Tamil Nadu in 1969.
 
• Its task was to examine the entire question concerning state autonomy and the Centre-State relations.
 
• The committee recommended a drastic overhaul of India’s federal system, with suggestions for the constitution to emerge as a truly federal one rather than quasi-federal.
 
• The need for such changes arose because of the contention that centralization of power diminishes the effectiveness of regional governments.
 
 
 
• **Balwant Rai Mehta Committee:**
 
 
• The Balwant Rai Mehta Committee was a committee appointed by the Government of India in 1957.
 
• The aim of this Committee was to examine the working of the Community Development Programme (1952) and the National Extension Service (1953) and to suggest measures for their better working.
 
• Significantly, their recommendations led to the birth of Panchayati Raj Institutions in India, outlining a three-tier system, including village, block, and district levels.
 
• The report of the Balwant Rai Mehta Committee is considered a landmark in the evolution of local self-government (Panchayati Raj) institutions in India.

questions.question: Pepperonil, ethyl acetate, butyraldehyde and nitrate are some common adulterants used in:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**ice cream.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Ice cream**, a popular dessert, has been subjected to adulteration with substances like **pepper oil, ethyl acetate, butyraldehyde, and nitrate. **These are used to **enhance the product's flavour** or replace more costly natural ingredients.
 
• **Pepper oil (or Pepperonil) **is sometimes used in ice cream **to add spiciness or a distinctive flavour.** It's a highly aromatic substance extracted from black pepper.
 
• **Ethyl Acetate** is a common solvent that is often used in the food industry as a **flavouring agent.** It is used in ice creams **to give a fruity flavour** or as a cheap alternative to real fruit.
 
• **Butyraldehyde** is an organic compound that has a powerful odour. In the food industry, it is used as a flavouring agent where it imparts **a buttery or creamy flavour**, providing a rich taste to ice cream.
 
• The use of such adulterants in food products like ice cream is often **regulated by food safety agencies. **While they can enhance flavour, they should only be used within permissible limits to ensure they're safe for consumption.
